findings.title: Stored XSS: embed URL interpolated unescaped into raw HTML post
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import builds the post body with `contents << "...#{url}..."` without any HTML escaping, and the resulting post is stored with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw verbatim, bypassing the markdown/sanitization pipeline). The `url` here is the user-supplied `embed_url` request parameter (only checked with a /^https?:\/\// regex), so a URL containing a single quote and a `, is injected into the post body and rendered unsanitized. The embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked`, so any visitor of the embedded page is exposed to stored XSS. The URL must be escaped (CGI.escapeHTML / ERB::Util.html_escape) and ideally validated with URI.parse.

findings.title: request.referer interpolated unescaped into inline JavaScript
findings.body: The layout embeds `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. The controller only validates that the referer's *host* equals embeddable_host; the path/query of the referring URL is attacker-influenced (any page on the embeddable host, or a crafted referer with quotes). A referer containing a single quote or `</script>` breaks out of the JS string literal, allowing script injection into the embed iframe's DOM. Use `escape_javascript`/json encoding for the value instead of raw ERB interpolation.

findings.title: create_table with force: true will silently drop an existing table
findings.body: The migration uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating. If this migration runs against a database that already has topic_embeds data (e.g. it was created outside migrations, or a partial deploy happened), all rows are silently destroyed. The same problem is introduced in this PR by changing db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb to `force: true`, which can drop production top_topics data on environments where the table already exists. `force: true` should only ever be used in development/test schemas, never in shipped migrations.

findings.title: poll_feed crashes when a feed item has no content element
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a `content` element. SimpleRSS returns nil for missing elements, so any feed item that only provides `description` (or an Atom feed without content) raises NoMethodError on nil. Since the job has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the whole hourly poll is aborted at the first such item and no further items are imported. Guard with `i.content || i.description` and handle nil.

findings.title: Import crashes if the existing embed's post has been deleted
findings.body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` may be nil (topic/post deleted by moderators, which is common for spam), and the next line calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` on nil, raising NoMethodError. PollFeed runs hourly and TopicRetriever calls it inline, so a single deleted post for a feed URL permanently breaks feed polling for all items after it (retry disabled). Handle a nil post by recreating the topic or skipping.

findings.title: No error handling around feed fetch; network error kills scheduled job with retry disabled
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` can raise OpenURI::HTTPError, SocketError, timeouts, or RSS parse errors. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, any transient network failure silently aborts the poll until the next hour with no logging. Wrap the fetch/parse in begin/rescue with logging so transient errors don't go unnoticed.

findings.title: Anonymous requests can trigger unauthenticated enqueues of retrieval jobs
findings.body: Any request passing the referer check (which only checks the host header of the referer, trivially spoofable via server-side fetch or a page on the host) with arbitrary embed_url values enqueues a RetrieveTopic job per unique URL. Although TopicRetriever throttles per-URL to once per 60s, an attacker can rotate unlimited distinct embed_url values (all on the embeddable host), each spawning a job that performs an outbound HTTP fetch (or a full PollFeed run) — a job-queue and outbound-traffic amplification vector with no global rate limit.

findings.title: import_remote does not restrict scheme, enabling file:// reads
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, but import_remote calls `open(url)` *before* that check, and Ruby's open-uri follows `file://` (and other schemes via redirects). The embed_url comes from the public controller via the RetrieveTopic job. Although TopicRetriever.invalid_host? compares hosts first, a URL like `file:///etc/passwd` has host nil != embeddable_host and is rejected there; however any code path calling import_remote directly (e.g. the disqus thor task with feed data) passes the URL straight to open(). Use an explicit http(s) check before open(), not just inside import.

findings.title: Weak origin check on postMessage handler
findings.body: The receiver validates messages with `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, an unanchored substring test. Any string merely *containing* the discourse origin passes (e.g. an origin like `http://discourse.example.com.attacker.tld` if the forum URL is a substring of it), and the check compares the full URL string against only the origin scheme+host. Use `e.origin === new URL(discourseUrl).origin` for an exact comparison. Impact is limited (message only sets iframe height), but it should be an exact check.

findings.title: feed_key is defined but never used, so polling has no modified/etag check
findings.body: The job defines `feed_key` (apparently intended for caching feed modified state) but never reads or writes it, and poll_feed re-imports every item on every hourly run, re-fetching and re-parsing each item's page via TopicEmbed.import (dedup is by embed_url, so content changes are re-imported even when the feed hasn't changed). Either wire the key into the polling logic or remove it; as-is it is dead code and the comment-implied caching behavior does not exist.
